extracted.intended_audience: abstractors, patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent office staff preparing abstracts of patent documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for drafting concise technical abstracts for patent documents that enable rapid assessment of the disclosure; covers presentation, length, content, and subject-matter-specific items to include. Intended to be followed irrespective of the receiving authority while noting authority-specific regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract of a patent document is a concise statement of its technical disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should enable the reader, regardless of familiarity with patent documents, to ascertain quickly the character of the subject matter and to decide whether to consult the full patent document. It is an efficient scanning tool for searching in the technical field. The abstract serves only for technical information and must not be used to interpret the scope of protection sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be clear and as concise as the disclosure permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the abstract should not exceed 250 words and preferably be in the range of 50 to 150 words. It may contain chemical or mathematical formulae and tables. Avoid phrases that can be implied (e.g., “This disclosure concerns”, “This invention relates to”) and avoid legal claim-style phraseology often used in claims (e.g., 'said', 'means'). Draft wording with any authority-specific requirements (e.g., inclusion of drawings) in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be primarily directed to that which is new in the art to which the invention pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention is a modification of an apparatus, process, product or composition, direct the abstract to the technical disclosure of the modification. If the invention is basic in nature and the entire disclosure is new, direct the abstract to the entire disclosure. When a patent document relating to a product also contains significant disclosure of method of preparation or use, abstract those matters as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle alternatives disclosed in the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure involves alternatives, the abstract should deal with the preferred alternative and identify the others if this can be done succinctly; if this cannot be done succinctly, state that alternatives exist and whether they differ substantially from the preferred alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter-specific minimum content (machine/article/compound/mixture/process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable and where the document contains the information, the abstract should include at least the following items depending on the type of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Machine, apparatus, or system: its organization and operation. (2) Article: its method of making. (3) Chemical compound: its identity and preparation. (4) Mixture: its ingredients. (5) Process: the steps. Note: Extensive mechanical and design details of apparatus should not be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and process exemplification and formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for abstracts of chemical compounds, compositions and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the general nature of the compound or composition and its use (e.g., class and intended use). Exemplify a class by a typical example. For processes, state the type of reaction, reagents and process conditions and generally illustrate by a single example. Wherever applicable, give the chemical formula which best characterizes the invention among the formulae contained in the patent document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of value claims and speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should not contain statements on the alleged merits, value, or speculative applications of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting advantages, benefits or speculative uses; keep the abstract factual and descriptive of the technical disclosure only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority-specific drawing/figure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider authority regulations regarding inclusion of drawings or figures with the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some authorities require that where the application contains drawings the abstract shall include a figure of the drawings or be accompanied by one or more figures on publication. In such cases draft the abstract with that requirement in mind (i.e., refer succinctly to the relevant drawing figure(s) if appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist per invention type
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a checklist to verify inclusion of required elements per invention type when preparing the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items include: For an article — identity, use, construction/organization, method of manufacture. For a chemical compound — identity (structure if appropriate), method of preparation, properties, uses. For a mixture — nature, properties, use, essential ingredients (identify, function), proportions if significant, preparation. For a machine/apparatus/system — nature, use, construction, organization, operation. For a process/operation — nature and characterizing features, material and conditions employed, product if significant, nature of and relationship between steps if more than one. Also use the checklist to confirm word count (<250; preferably 50–150).
